llm.summary: This is a disclosed Chinese educational prompt-template skill, with no executable code, network behavior, persistence, credential access, or hidden high-impact actions found.

dimensions.detail: The declared tools are Read, Write, Edit, and AskUserQuestion, but the instructions only require reading bundled reference files, asking for missing title details, and producing prompt text; there is no instruction to access private files, credentials, sessions, or external services.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown documentation only; no installer, executable scripts, dependency setup, remote payload retrieval, or runtime bootstrap was present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger list includes broad style and fandom terms, and the skill defaults generated text to Chinese; both are disclosed and aligned with the Chinese CSP-J educational-card purpose, but users should be aware of possible broad activation and language bias.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, memory modification, background work, privilege escalation, tool wrapping, destructive action, or credential handling was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts coherently describe a prompt generator for notebook-style educational knowledge cards, with supporting Markdown references for styles, layouts, examples, and C++ contest-code formatting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Installers should expect this skill to generate Chinese-first educational image prompts and to activate on several broad visual-style keywords. It appears low-risk from a security standpoint because it ships only Markdown guidance and does not request credentials, run code, fetch remote content, or persist changes.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger terms are tied to the skill's supported visual themes such as anime, Minecraft, and pixel styles. This may reduce activation precision, but it does not introduce hidden authority or unsafe behavior.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-language default appears throughout the skill and examples, including the explicit Chinese-priority principle. This is disclosed and coherent for Chinese CSP-J educational materials, though users wanting another language should request it explicitly.
[P9] expected: The whitespace hits occur in aligned Markdown tables in styles.md. Manual inspection showed table padding around visible style rows, not concealed instructions or prompt-injection content.
